doc.title: Phil Woods interviewed by Monk Rowe, Delaware Water Gap, PA, November 8, 1999

title: Stravinsky tone row in the Sun Suite and RCA freedom
summary: Woods says a Stravinsky tone row sparked part of the suite and praises RCA's big budget and free rein.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well this piece, the string parts you said you were inspired or emulating Stravinsky in a sense.

I used the melody from the first [scats] that’s the tone row from one of Stravinsky’s early serial pieces. I used to know the name of it but I’m just blanking out. But I found the tone row anyway and that sparked that part of the piece.
Do you remember when you recorded it if it sounded like you thought it was going to?
Yeah, I was very pleased with it. So nice to have a project like that.
Big budget, and free reign to do what you want. Yeah RCA was good in those days.
